A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QCAI and TCR-XAI study. The complete main text and Appendices A–C are readable, and matching text, equations, tables, and rendered figures supports a reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, perturbation experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and structural case studies. Appendix A.12 also reports original CLIP classification results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, perturbation, ablation, runtime, and case-study results, including the CLIP experiment in Appendix A.12.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical query and key attribution procedures, pseudoinverse operations, and layer aggregation rules. The model-specific losses in Appendix A.4 and CLIP adaptation in Appendix A.12 are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 274-complex TCR-XAI benchmark, VDJdb/IEDB/McPAS-TCR data, and 73,000-image MS-COCO subset. The new introduction reference to Appendix A.12 points to an existing vision-language experiment, not added coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4 retains AttnLRP, TokenTM, AttCAT, Rollout, GradCAM, LRP, and RawAttn. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the integrated-dataset, runtime, ablation, and case-study comparisons.

E3.justification: Distance thresholds, importance-score smoothing, perturbation thresholds, BRHR evaluation, and confidence-based grouping remain unchanged. Appendix A.12 retains the 65,700/7,300 training/test split and 100 training epochs.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same maximum-versus-average and cross-versus-self-attention ablations, threshold sensitivity studies, training-similarity and prediction-outcome analyses, and structural and CLIP case studies. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 4 and 5 retain the same plus/minus and parenthesized variability reporting. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and graphical findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains QCAI's CDR3b LOdds of -3.498 and AOPC of 0.045; Appendix A.12 retains 94.08% accuracy and 0.9997 ROC-AUC.

T1.justification: The attention definitions, pseudoinverse derivation, and aggregation equations in Sections 2–3 are unchanged, as are the BRHR definition and Appendix A.3.1 task formalization. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or reasoning are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve the same contributions and performance claims concerning QCAI, TCR-XAI, and BRHR. The added Appendix A.12 pointer does not expand the applicability claim already supported and discussed in v2.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same justification for physical distance as an importance proxy, interpretation of cross-attention's contribution, caveat about sequence changes affecting explanations, and future directions involving energy metrics and explain-by-design models.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces the description of a supplied code package and planned public release with explicit project-website and GitHub source-code locations, also added to the main text. It removes the earlier weight-retrieval guidance and trained-weight release promise. Implementation and hardware details remain unchanged; trained-weight availability is not established.

R1.justification: The duplicate BERT preprint reference is consolidated into the retained publication, NetTCR-2.2 receives publication metadata, and the Vaswani author list is corrected. These concern the same cited works; the literature coverage and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgments, code-availability text, and publication headers, alongside limited wording edits, an Appendix A.12 cross-reference, and bibliographic cleanup. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The publication headers, title-page link, and added code and acknowledgment text cause limited reflow, including references spilling onto an additional page. All 14 figures and 13 tables retain their content, captions, and display structure.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation by replacing a future public-release statement with explicit code locations, correcting bibliographic records, and improving navigation to the existing CLIP appendix. Removing weight-specific guidance limits the reproducibility benefit, and trained-weight availability remains unspecified. The scientific method, evidence, and limitations are unchanged.
